‘Enemy Of Islam Wants To Sow Division...’: Mojtaba Khamenei’s Message To Gulf Rulers
Iran’s Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei urged Gulf rulers to strengthen Muslim unity, cooperation and security, warning that forces opposed to Islam seek to exploit divisions among Muslim nations.
- Iranian leader Mojtaba Khamenei urged Muslim nations to unite.
- Khamenei warned external forces exploit differences to divide Muslims.
- He urged Gulf rulers to enhance cooperation and security.
- This message comes amidst high tensions in West Asia.

In his message, Khamenei said differences among Muslims based on race, culture, society, economy, politics and geography should not become a reason for division.
Khamenei said forces opposed to Islam seek to exploit these differences to weaken Muslims. According to him, such forces are constantly looking for opportunities to widen divisions between Muslim countries and strengthen their own influence.

He also appealed to the rulers of Gulf countries to understand the circumstances around them and identify the forces he considers the “real enemies” of Muslims.

Mojtaba Khamenei said the solutions to challenges faced by the Islamic nations lay in “friendship” and “cooperation.”
Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei on Sunday urged countries in West Asia to unite against their enemy. In a written message issued six months after the start of the war in West Asia began, Mojtaba called on countries to “recognise your real enemy, understand its plan, and confront it”, while referring to the United States and Israel.
He said the solutions to challenges faced by the Islamic nations lay in “friendship” and “cooperation.” Mojtaba became the Supreme Leader shortly after his father Ali Khamenei was killed at the start of the war by US-Israeli strikes.
He has not made any public address since his appointment, and authorities have not released any video or audio of him. However, Mojtaba has, from time to time, released written statements which have been aired by Iran's state television.

‘Anyone who creates division among Muslims serves purpose of enemies’
In his message on the day Shia Muslims marked the birthday of the Prophet Mohammed, Mojtaba said those who create conflict among Muslims “serve the purpose of enemies.”
“Anyone, in any position, who does anything that leads to division among Muslims and creates conflict in the Muslim community, knowingly or unknowingly, intentionally or unintentionally, has served the purpose of the enemies of Islam,” he said, according to his official website.
He further added, “The solution to the problems of the Islamic nations is unity of words, friendship, and cooperation on the path of goodness.”

corpus.title: US Testing Giant Suspends TOEFL, GRE Exams In Iran After Sanctions
corpus.signal_text:
Khamenei Calls On Muslim States To Unite Against US, Israel
A written message attributed to Iran’s supreme leader, Mojtaba Khamenei, was posted on his Telegram channel on August 30 calling on Muslim countries to unite against what he described as their “real enemy,” the United States and Israel.
The message was published as part of the Islamic Unity Week, which marks the birthday of the Prophet Muhammad.
It urged Gulf rulers to unite against the United States and Israel. Many Gulf Arab monarchies view Tehran as a threat and host US forces. During the war, Iran struck US military sites and other infrastructure in several of those countries.
Khamenei has not been seen in public since being reportedly injured in US-Israeli air strikes half a year ago that killed his father and previous supreme leader, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei.
No audio or video comments from him have been released since the war started in late February, raising questions about his physical condition.
Many unverified reports state that he was badly disfigured with US President Donald Trump saying on August 27 that he believed Khamenei was still alive but “very seriously wounded.”
The latest message comes only days after another message attributed to Khamenei was issued that called to ban any “expressions of weakness” that would "harm social cohesion" in Iran and be a "great help to the enemy" as US sanctions continue to hit the country.
US Testing Giant Suspends TOEFL, GRE Exams In Iran After Sanctions
The Educational Testing Service (ETS) has confirmed in a written statement to RFE/RL’s Radio Farda that it has suspended the Test of English as a Foreign Language (TOEFL) in Iran in line with the latest US sanctions on the country.
The ETS is a US-based nonprofit that designs and runs standardized tests.
The move comes days after the language-learning company Duolingo said its English test was unavailable in Iran and to users with Iranian identification.
ETS said that “following OFAC's (Office of Foreign Assets Control) suspension of General License G, ETS has paused administration of the TOEFL and GRE (Graduate Record Examination) tests in Iran effective immediately. This step reflects our full compliance with US sanctions law. Test takers affected by this pause will be contacted directly.”
Both the TOEFL and the GRE, a standardized test used for admission to many graduate programs, are often required of international students applying to universities in Western countries.
